## When to Use
Use for task-319794d9 instances where a complete color-2 row/column is adjacent to a separate colored shape, and demonstrations indicate a full-length color-8 parallel stripe beyond that shape.

# Task 319794d9: extend a full-line shadow past an adjacent object

## Validated rule
The input contains a complete straight line of color 2 and a separate colored shape immediately adjacent to one side of that line. Keep both the line and the shape exactly where they are. Add a complete parallel line of color 8 immediately beyond the shape's far edge, on the side away from the color-2 line. The new color-8 line spans the entire grid dimension parallel to the original line (not merely the object's size/cross-section). Preserve all other cells.

- For a vertical color-2 line, identify the adjacent object's farthest column away from the line; put color 8 in the next column, from top to bottom.
- For a horizontal color-2 line, identify the adjacent object's farthest row away from the line; put color 8 in the next row, across the full width.
- Shape may occupy only part of the dimension parallel to the full line. The output stripe nevertheless covers the full dimension.
- Do not move the object. This is distinct from object-motion/trail tasks.

## Demonstration evidence

6. Confirmed translation variant (task instance solved): the test was 28×13 with a full-width color-2 row at row 0 and a color-3 L-shaped object at rows 3–5, columns 1–3, with occupied offsets `[(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(1,2),(2,2)]`. Correct output slides the L upward by 2 rows so its top touches the color-2 line (object now at rows 1–3, same columns), and adds a full-width color-8 row at row 4, immediately beyond the object's far edge. All other cells remain background color 7. This was supported by a demo: 8×8 with a full-height color-2 line at column 3 and a 2×8 color-6 rectangle at columns 5–6; output slides the rectangle one column left to columns 4–5 so it touches the 2-line, then places a full-height color-8 stripe at column 6 (the object's one-column trailing strip). Therefore, in this movement variant, translate the entire object toward the full 2-line until touching, and put an 8 stripe immediately on its far side; the stripe covers the whole dimension parallel to the 2-line, while preserving the translated object's shape/color.

**Do not confuse this confirmed movement variant with cases where the object stays put and a full-length stripe is added at an inferred boundary.** Here, use the demo's explicit object translation; infer movement distance by making the nearest edge touch the 2-line, and put the trail stripe immediately beyond the object's far edge. In the L test, this required moving two rows and the 8 row at row 4; in the rectangle demo, moving one column and the 8 column at column 6.

1. 27x14 grid: full vertical 2-line at column 5 (0-based); a color-1 rectangle at column 4, rows 10–18. Output added a full-height color-8 line at column 3; line and rectangle stayed fixed.
2. 23x22 grid: full horizontal 2-line at row 20; a color-7 irregular shape occupies rows 14–19 and touches the line. Output added a full-width color-8 line at row 13; the color-7 shape and 2-line stayed fixed.
3. Solved test: 10x19 grid with vertical 2-line at column 1 and a small color-7 L shape at rows 6–7, columns 2–3. Correct output was a full-height color-8 line at column 4; all input cells remained unchanged otherwise.

4. 25x27 grid: full vertical 2-line at column 26; a color-5 shape occupies rows 16–17, columns 23–25, touching the line at column 25. Correct output adds a full-height color-8 line at column 22, immediately beyond the shape's far edge; all input cells remain unchanged.
5. Confirmed on a 17x11 test: full vertical 2-line at column 9; a 1-shape at rows 2–7, columns 7–8. Correct output adds a full-height 8-line at column 6; the input line and shape remain unchanged.

## Additional confirmed solved instance and caution
A 16x7 test had a full horizontal color-2 row at row 3 (0-based), and a separate three-cell horizontal color-4 object at row 9, columns 2-4. The correct output preserved the input and added a full-width color-8 row at row 5 (0-based), two rows below the full color-2 line; it did NOT place the 8 stripe beyond the object's far edge. This is inconsistent with a simple universal rule that always puts the stripe immediately past the object's far edge. The task's demonstrated cases may have additional selection/placement structure; after an incorrect submission, do not keep applying the far-edge rule mechanically. Recompare the exact full-line/object geometry and, if needed, request a discriminating demo before another attempt.

## New evidence: line and broad object on opposite sides
A solved 9x28 instance has full-width color-2 row 1, with a broad irregular color-6 object occupying rows 5-6. Correct output leaves original cells unchanged and adds a full-width color-8 row 4, immediately above the object's nearest edge (the object is below the full line). This was established after rejecting stripes at rows 3, 7, and an attempted move of the object. Three demos establish directional placement behavior: (a) a full-height 2-line at column 4 with an adjacent 4-rectangle on its left added a full-height 8-line at column 1, the far-side edge of the 4-rectangle; (b) full-height 2-line at column 22 with 7-rectangle at columns 12-20 added 8-line at column 12 (left edge of object), not at far edge; (c) a full-width 2-row at row 12 and a 5-object in rows 7-9 added 8-row at row 8, overwriting that row of the object with a full-width stripe. The new case adds an 8-row at row 4, just before the object. Exact selection/placement remains nontrivial: don't assume stripe is always far edge or always beyond the object. For broad objects, useful observed placement is the leading/nearest boundary row or column (facing the 2-line), sometimes stripe overlays part of object. After a failed attempt, request demos and compare exact geometry before retrying.
## Additional confirmed solved test
An 11x9 test had a full vertical color-2 line at column 8 and a single color-6 cell at row 3, column 7. Correct output preserved all input cells and added a full-height color-8 stripe at column 6, immediately beyond the object's far edge away from the 2-line.

## Validation checklist
- Confirm color 2 forms a complete row or column.
- Identify the separate object and its relation to the full line; do not assume it touches the line.
- Infer the stripe's exact location from all available examples. Prior examples often add a full-length color-8 stripe beyond the object's far edge, but the confirmed 16x7 case instead puts it at row 5, two rows below the full line.
- Extend the stripe across the entire dimension parallel to the full line.
- Preserve the input object and full color-2 line; preserve every other cell unless evidence establishes overwriting.
- Ensure output dimensions match input.
